primary_diagnosis_treated: Acute decompensated heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
nice_guideline_used: NG106 (Chronic heart failure in adults: diagnosis and management)

medications.dose: 20 mg PO once daily (titrate by 20‑40 mg qd to achieve euvolemia)
medications.duration: Titrate to euvolemia, then ongoing – review weekly
medications.purpose: Rapid relief of congestion in acute decompensated HFpEF
medications.nice_justification: NG106 recommends loop diuretics as first‑line for fluid overload

medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and after any renal function change
medications.purpose: Disease‑modifying therapy for HFpEF; reduces HF hospitalisation and CV death
medications.nice_justification: NG106 (TA902/TA929) recommends SGLT2‑inhibitors for all HF patients regardless of diabetes

medications.dose: 25 mg PO once daily (consider uptitration to 50 mg if BP and renal function allow)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review BP and renal function after any dose change
medications.purpose: RAAS blockade for hypertension, CKD, IHD and HFpEF
medications.nice_justification: NG106 lists ARB as first‑line when ACE‑I intolerant or as part of HF regimen

medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate to target HR <70 bpm
medications.purpose: Rate control and mortality reduction in IHD/HFpEF
medications.nice_justification: NG106 recommends beta‑blockers for stable HF patients (not during acute decompensation)

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of ischemic heart disease
medications.nice_justification: CG126 recommends lifelong low‑dose aspirin for IHD
CG126/NG185 advise 12‑month dual antiplatelet after ACS

medications.duration: Lifelong – review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of cardiovascular events in IHD
medications.nice_justification: CG126 recommends high‑intensity statin for all patients with established IHD

interactions_checked.interaction: Duplicate β‑blockade leading to bradycardia and excessive β‑blockade
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue metoprolol tartrate 25 mg; continue metoprolol succinate only

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive diuretic effect may cause hypotension, volume depletion, electrolyte disturbances
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure, weight, serum electrolytes and creatinine after initiation and after any dose change

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined effect on renal perfusion may increase creatinine
interactions_checked.action: Check renal function and potassium 1‑2 weeks after any dose change
Continue dual therapy for 12 months post‑STEMI; monitor for signs of bleeding

contraindications.reason: Duplicate β‑blocker with metoprolol succinate; risk of excessive β‑blockade and bradycardia
contraindications.alternative: Continue metoprolol succinate 100 mg ER only

contraindications.reason: Patient has CKD stage 3‑4; NSAIDs worsen renal function and cause fluid retention
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol for analgesia; avoid NSAIDs

contraindications.reason: Fluid retention risk in heart failure and CKD
Negative inotropes contraindicated in heart failure
Dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalaemia and AKI risk; patient already on ARB
contraindications.alternative: Do not add ACE‑I while on losartan

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² to allow dapagliflozin and ARB use; will verify before initiation
Blood pressure not provided – assumed not hypotensive; will measure before titrating losartan or adding dapagliflozin
No documented sulfonamide allergy – assumed safe for dapagliflozin; will confirm with patient
Baseline liver function tests not provided – assumed normal for high‑intensity atorvastatin; will obtain LFTs before start
Duplicate beta‑blocker identified; plan to discontinue metoprolol tartrate
treatment_summary: Initiate loop diuretic (furosemide) and SGLT2‑inhibitor (dapagliflozin) for acute congestion and disease‑modifying benefit in HFpEF, continue ARB (losartan) and beta‑blocker (metoprolol succinate) for RAAS blockade and rate control, and maintain dual antiplatelet therapy for 12 months post‑STEMI. Switch to high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg and discontinue duplicate metoprolol tartrate and the two lower‑dose statins. Continue necessary inhalers, memantine, vitamin B12, and nitroglycerin PRN. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, BP, weight, and bleeding risk per NICE NG106 and CG126 recommendations.
